AlternateTargets: lord and minister in the Five Ranks
Senses.Explanation: The Caodong technical configuration of lord and minister. The term occurs 960 times in 217 allowlisted texts. Caoshan maps the lord to the upright position and the minister to the crooked, then names minister-facing-lord, lord-regarding-minister, and lord-and-minister-in-accord (君為正位。臣為偏位). Another record equates the final relation with arriving within both, while a direct answer identifies the Caodong house by “lord and minister in accord” (君臣道合). A house comparison sets this five-position configuration beside Linji’s three mysteries and three essentials. A later text disputes whether Caoshan originally arranged the answers as a separate fivefold set; that is an attested historical disagreement about classification, not a reason to remove the technical configuration.
Senses.Note: Primary Caodong sense. Cross-check the broader Five Ranks entry (五位); prince, upright-crooked, and merit rank systems remain related families rather than extra senses here. The Zen deviation is the conversion of political hierarchy into named rank relations and a house-identifying answer.

Occurrences.Kwic: 君為正位。臣為偏位。臣向君是偏中正。君視臣是正中偏。君臣道合是兼帶語。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: (撫州曹山元證禪師語錄) (Caoshan Benji's recorded sayings); the master's answer (師曰, 'the master said') to a monk's question about the essential formula of the five positions of lord and minister (僧問五位君臣旨訣) — the canonical mapping of (君)/(臣) onto (正)/(偏) and the three relational ranks.

Occurrences.Kwic: 君為正位，臣乃偏位，臣向君是偏中正，君視臣是正中偏，君臣道合
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Independent witness quoting Caoshan (frame 豈不見曹山道：…, 'have you not seen Caoshan say: …') inside another master's discourse; same definition, so MasterName=null (quotation).

Occurrences.Kwic: 兼中到者，即君臣道合也。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: (天界覺浪盛禪師語錄) (Juelang Daosheng's yulu); the passage sits under the governing heads (洞宗標正) ('setting upright the Dong lineage') → (洞曹君臣正偏及功勳父子主賓五位參同宗旨) ('the concordant purport of the Dongshan-Caoshan lord-minister, upright-crooked, merit, father-son, and host-guest five positions') — the named master's own teaching words (法語) essay expounding the five-position (五位) cross-mapping (正中偏=君視臣, 偏中正=臣向君, 兼中到=君臣道合). Juelang Daosheng (覺浪道盛) is in master-dates.json, so per the governing-section-head rule MasterName=Juelang Daosheng.

Occurrences.Kwic: 如何是曹洞宗？」師云：「君臣道合。」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: (君臣道合) ('lord and minister in accord') given as the one-line emblem of the Caodong house in a catechism on the essential principles of the five houses (五家宗旨); two-speaker Q&A (the follow-on questioner 進云 'he went on to ask' asks, the master 師 answers), so MasterName=null per the two-speaker rule. The answering master is determinate — the text is (天隱和尚語錄) (Tianyin Yuanxiu; attribution line 明 圓修說, 'spoken by Yuanxiu, Ming dynasty'; in master-dates.json).

Occurrences.Kwic: 曹山就話荅話，當面具陳，初未嘗與五位為配。後人不辯，以此為君臣五位語
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The intra-corpus dispute: the author argues (君臣) was answered ad hoc by Caoshan and only later mislabelled a separate (君臣五位) scheme. Meaning of (君)=(正)/(臣)=(偏) is not contested.

Occurrences.Kwic: 謂具三玄三要者，覿體全真；謂分五位君臣者，宛轉回互。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A house-device comparison sets the three mysteries and essentials beside the five lord-minister positions, which are described as winding through mutual interchange.

Senses.Explanation: The ordinary political and ethical roles of lord and minister. Two allowlisted discourses place their duty beside affection between father and son, distinctions between spouses, age order, and trust among friends (君臣有義). These are social roles, not the Caodong rank configuration.
Senses.Note: Ordinary corpus-wide sense. Kept separate because actual political/ethical persons and a technical rank schema are different things.

Occurrences.Kwic: 父子有親，君臣有義，夫婦有別，長幼有序，朋友有信。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A discourse lists affection between father and son, duty between lord and minister, distinction between spouses, age order, and trust between friends.
